claims.text: Adding 1–2 at% Al to FeNiCrCoCu will promote in-situ formation of a robust protective oxide during high-temperature sliding.
The protective oxide governs overall wear resistance.
The protective oxide minimizes microscopic plastic deformation through tribo-oxide-mediated load transfer.
The baseline coating has a homogeneous, well-characterized microstructure.
A controlled Al addition of 1–2 at% is the proposed change relative to the Al-free coating.
The predicted behavior applies during oxidizing sliding at approximately 700–800 °C with sufficient oxygen partial pressure for oxide formation.
Al stabilizes a more robust and continuous oxide layer under high-temperature sliding conditions.
The oxide layer acts as a barrier to direct metal-to-metal contact.
The oxide layer facilitates load transfer during sliding.
Oxide-mediated separation and load transfer reduce abrasive and adhesive wear.
Oxide-mediated separation and load transfer limit localized plastic deformation.
The Al-modified coating will have a lower wear rate than the Al-free baseline.
The Al-modified coating will exhibit less microscopic plastic deformation than the Al-free baseline.
Under the same oxidizing high-temperature sliding conditions, the Al-free baseline forms a less stable and possibly discontinuous oxide layer.
At lower temperatures or in inert atmospheres, limited oxide formation may eliminate the predicted improvement in wear and deformation resistance.
Tribo-oxide mediation is supported by analogous material systems.
